decisionBox.changed: REDUCE becomes ADD, and the reason is that the desk's own written level fired against its own written bias. This morning published a bearish 22/34/44 book, reduced 25 percent of spot at 76,954.5, and set an add gate at 77,056.0 that it did not expect to see. The 13:00Z hourly closed 77,174.9 - through the gate, four minutes after publication - and price has spent the five hours since building a higher base rather than failing back. Honouring a gate you wrote and did not want is the entire point of writing gates down, so the wallet adds. What has NOT changed is the tilt: the bias moves bearish to range-with-bearish-tilt, not to bullish, because the bounce has not reclaimed a single 1H or 4H moving average and positioning got WORSE while price went up. The stop order stays off - spot is 743.1 points above the reduce level, and the overnight decision belongs to endday.

calibration.rollingRecord: Morning 10 September went 1-for-2 on its written gates and the miss is the instructive one. The 76,680.0 reduce gate did NOT fire: the lowest settled hourly close after publication was 76,902.0 at 12:00Z, and the 13:00Z bar low of 76,736.1 came within 56.1 points of the level without closing through it. The 77,056.0 add gate DID fire, on the very next settled bar - the 13:00Z hourly closed 77,174.9, 118.9 points above it, four minutes after the report went out. Morning itself wrote that a gate 0.15 ATRs away 'will probably fire'; it was talking about the reduce, and it was the add that went instead. Yesterday's endday remains 3-for-3 by contrast.
calibration.note: acting_helped is FALSE and the desk should own it plainly. Morning sold 25 percent of the spot core at 76,954.5 into what it called a bounce inside a live cascade; spot is now 77,423.1, so that quarter was sold 468.6 points below the current mark and the reduce cost roughly 0.29 USDT against having done nothing. The reasoning was not lazy - record long crowding, rising open interest, hostile macro, a book that was 98.8 percent long with 2.25 USDT of cash - and every one of those observations is still true and has in fact got worse. What was wrong was the sequencing: the desk acted on a bearish thesis at the exact moment its own add gate was about to fire, which means the gate and the thesis were pointing opposite ways and the thesis won. The transferable rule is the inverse of yesterday's stop lesson. Yesterday taught that a written level beats a pattern you have grown attached to. Today teaches the same thing from the other side: when the level and the narrative disagree, the level is the one you wrote down when you were calm. This report acts on the fired gate.
